brief: How to protect 4 hours of deep work in a calendar full of meetings.

slots.headline: How to Protect Four Hours of Deep Work Daily

slots.title: Audit Your Calendar
slots.body: Review your current schedule and identify low-value meetings. Cancel or delegate anything that doesn't require your expertise. Reclaiming this time is the first step toward focused work.

slots.title: Block Deep Work
slots.body: Schedule a recurring four-hour daily block as a non-negotiable appointment. Treat this commitment with the same respect as any client meeting. Protecting this window trains others to honor your focus.

slots.title: Defend Your Mornings
slots.body: Reserve your peak cognitive hours for demanding tasks before noon. Meetings drain mental energy, so push collaborative calls to afternoons. This rhythm maximizes output when your mind is sharpest.

slots.title: Set Clear Boundaries
slots.body: Communicate your focus hours to teammates and update your status. Use calendar titles like Deep Work to signal unavailability clearly. Boundaries only work when they are visible and consistent.

slots.title: Batch Meetings Together
slots.body: Cluster calls into one or two dedicated days to preserve focus blocks. Context switching between deep work and meetings destroys productivity. A fragmented calendar guarantees shallow work wins.

slots.title: Review Weekly Ritual
slots.body: Spend fifteen minutes each Friday auditing next week's schedule. Look for intrusions and shift meetings before they erode your deep work. Consistent reviews turn protection into a lasting habit.
